steps.path: When the assistant wants to run an admin command (Ask first mode)
steps.headline: An admin command's approval card shows the exact command and has no Always Allow.
steps.changed: Today this card shows only the assistant's one-line summary and offers Always Allow. Now the exact command sits above Yes / No, Always Allow is gone, and a line says your password comes next.
steps.notice: You see precisely what you're approving before you say Yes, and you can never tell it to stop asking.

steps.path: The same, in Full auto mode
steps.headline: Full auto's stop for an admin command also shows the exact command, with no Always Allow.
steps.changed: The existing 'Stopped before an admin command' band keeps its wording and Run it / Skip it. The exact command is added, and Always Allow is removed.
steps.notice: Full auto still stops for every admin command, and now shows you what it is.

steps.path: Right after you press Yes on an admin command
steps.headline: After Yes, a password box appears on the same command's card; the command runs once you press Run it.
steps.changed: A new part of the card: a heading, the admin step, a masked password box, Run it / Skip it, and a line promising it's never saved or shown to the assistant.
steps.notice: The typing cursor jumps into the password box, so a password can't end up in the message box by accident.
steps.risk: Run it stays dim until you type something.

steps.headline: A wrong password empties the box and says how many tries are left.
steps.changed: The same card stays up with the box cleared and a bold line: 'Wrong password. 2 tries left.'
steps.notice: A typo costs a retry, not a failed command.

steps.headline: Before the last try, the card warns that another wrong password may lock you out for about 10 minutes.
steps.changed: On the final try the line adds the lockout warning. Some Linux computers lock sudo for about 10 minutes after 3 wrong tries.
steps.notice: You're warned before the lockout happens, not after.

highlight.text: Wrong password. 1 try left. Another wrong one may lock you out of admin actions for about 10 minutes.

steps.path: A command you approved asks for admin partway through (an install script)
steps.headline: When a script asks for admin partway through, the card names the script and the exact step, and says to type only if expected.
steps.changed: Same card, with the line: 'Partway through, install.sh wants to run this with full control of your computer. Only type your password if you expected this step.'
steps.notice: Installers now work from chat, and you see the real admin step rather than just 'Run the install script'.
steps.risk: Can't be known before the command starts, so this card appears while the command is already running.

highlight.text: Partway through, install.sh wants to run this with full control of your computer. Only type your password if you expected this step:
